title: Reading Earth's Stacked Pages
question: How do geologists put Earth's rocks, and its history, in order?
hook: A cliff face is a stack of history, and a handful of simple rules tell you which layer came first.
idea: Rules about how rock layers stack and cut each other give their relative order, and dating methods then fix the ages of the boundaries.

beats.prompt: You find pebbles of limestone embedded inside a layer of sandstone. What does that tell you about the two rocks?

choices.label: The limestone formed first, then got caught up in the sandstone
The sandstone formed first, then grew the limestone inside it
choices.feedback: This reverses the order: the pebbles had to exist before the rock around them formed.

choices.label: Both rocks formed at exactly the same time
choices.feedback: Tempting because they sit together, but the pebbles were already solid rock when the sandstone formed around them.

choices.label: Their order cannot be told without fossils
choices.feedback: No fossils are needed here; the embedded pieces alone reveal which rock came first.

beats.explain: By the law of included fragments, pieces of one rock embedded in a second rock must have formed first and were included as the second rock formed.

beats.prompt: Match each principle to what it says.
pairs: Oldest layers lie at the bottom
Sediments are first laid down flat
A rock that cuts another is younger
Fossil sets follow a reliable order
beats.explain: Each principle lets geologists work out which rocks are older or younger without knowing their exact ages.

beats.prompt: Sort each into rock units (chronostratigraphic) or time units (geochronologic).
beats.explain: A system is the body of rock laid down during an interval; the matching period is the interval of time itself.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: The base of the Cambrian Period was once dated at 541 Ma.
In 2022, better dating revised that age to 538.8 Ma.
So the golden spike at the base of the Cambrian had to be moved to a different rock layer.
The boundary between the Ediacaran and Cambrian systems is still defined at the same point in the rock.
beats.explain: Improved dating changes the age of a time unit, but the rock definition of the boundary (its GSSP) stays where it is; only the absolute age is refined.
